en: Buddha-stotra: Om, homage to the Buddha;
homage be to the Buddha, the one of pure awakening.
For the sake of the awakening that is the manifestation of the pure Dharma;
for the subsequent awakening attained through the merit of the True Dharma;
for the emptiness of the peak of existence; and for the sake of pure awakening. || 1 ||
Aho! Aho! The Buddha of infinite splendor;
aho! aho! the ocean, Meru, and the forest grove;
aho! aho! the Buddha of infinite range.
It is as exceedingly rare as the flower of the Udumbara tree. || 2 ||
Oh, how great is the Tathāgata of great compassion! Oh, oh, the banner of the Śākya clan! Oh, how worthy of prostration is that sun among men!
By whom this supreme sūtra was thus spoken. || 3 ||
For the sake of favoring all sentient beings,
the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Lord of Peace, has surely taught the practice of the True Dharma.
The Supreme Being has entered the city of peace. || 4 ||
When the sphere of the Victorious Buddhas has entered the state of concentration that is profound, peaceful, and stainless,
then even the bodies of the Śrāvakas are empty.
The monasteries of the supreme among bipeds are empty. || 5 ||
All those phenomena are empty by nature;
for beings are indeed empty, and they have never existed at any time.
I remember the Jina constantly and constantly;
I long for the sight of the Jina constantly and constantly;
and I make my vow constantly and constantly.
And for the purpose of seeing him who is worthy of worship by the Perfectly Awakened One. || 7 ||
Placing his knees constantly upon the ground here, tormented by grief for the sake of seeing the Jina, you,
O compassionate Leader, [have come].
My thirst for the sight of the Sugata is exceedingly great. || 8 ||
O best among the virtuous, grant me the cool water of your vision, which you constantly bestow;
for beings are filled with longing to behold your form.
Gladden them with the water of your compassion.
O Protector, O Leader, manifest a state of compassion; grant me the sight of your gentle form. You are the savior, the sole teacher of the world; protect me!
And the bodies of the Śrāvakas are likewise empty. || 10 ||
Equal to space, having the nature of the sky, they are like an illusion, a mirage, or the moon reflected in water;
and all sentient beings have the nature of happiness.
May they be so, O Leader, through your grace. || 11 ||
The *Buddhastotra* named *Bodhisattvasamuccaya*, composed by Kuladevatā, is completed.
